item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 251754
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 AM PDT Tue Aug 25 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Lala, located several hundred miles north of Pearl and Hermes
Atoll, on Tropical Storm Iselle, located several hundred miles
west of the southern tip of the Baja California Peninsula, and on
Tropical Storm Julio, located well west-southwest of the southern
tip of Baja California Peninsula.

Central East Pacific:
A tropical wave located well to the south of southern Mexico is
producing a large area of showers and thunderstorms. This system
has become become better organized since yesterday, and
environmental conditions appear favorable for further development.
A tropical depression is expected to form in a few days while it
moves generally west-northwestward at 10 to 15 mph, well offshore
of Mexico.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...medium...40 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...90 percent.

Western East Pacific:
A trough of low pressure located well to the east-southeast of the
Hawaiian Islands is producing some disorganized showers and
thunderstorms. An area of low pressure is forecast to form along the
trough during the next couple of days, and environmental conditions
appear conducive for some gradual development thereafter. A tropical
depression is likely to form during the latter part of the week or
early this weekend while the system drifts northeastward, then
turns to the west-northwest.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...30 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...70 percent.

Well Offshore of Southern Mexico:
An area of low pressure could form well offshore of Central America
late this week or this weekend. Environmental conditions should
support some gradual development of this system, and a tropical
depression could form late this weekend or early next week while it
moves westward to west-northwestward at 10 to 15 mph well offshore
of southern Mexico.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...medium...50 percent.

Central Pacific:
An area of low pressure could form well south of the Hawaiian
Islands late this week. Some gradual development is possible by
the weekend into early next week while the system moves slowly to
the west or west-northwest, well south-southwest of the Hawaiian
Islands.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...20 percent.

$$
Forecaster Blake

item.title: Tropical Storm Iselle Public Advisory Number 10
item.description:
Issued at 200 PM PDT Tue Aug 25 2026 
000
WTPZ34 KNHC 252040
TCPEP4
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Iselle Advisory Number  10
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP092026
200 PM PDT Tue Aug 25 2026
 
...ISELLE LIKELY TO FURTHER WEAKEN THIS WEEK...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 200 PM PDT...2100 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...21.0N 121.8W
ABOUT 775 MI...1245 KM W OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...60 MPH...95 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...WNW OR 285 DEGREES AT 9 MPH...15 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...994 MB...29.36 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 200 PM PDT (2100 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Iselle was
located near latitude 21.0 North, longitude 121.8 West. Iselle is
moving toward the west-northwest near 9 mph (15 km/h), and this
general motion is expected for the next couple of days, with a turn
towards the west possible late on Wednesday.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 60 mph (95 km/h) with higher gusts.
Weakening is forecast, and Iselle could become a post-tropical 
cyclone on Wednesday.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 230 miles (370 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 994 mb (29.36 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
SURF: Swells generated by Iselle are affecting the west coast of the
Baja California Peninsula, and will continue for a couple more days.
These swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip
current conditions. Please consult products from your local weather
office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 800 PM PDT.
 
$$
Forecaster Blake/Evans

item.title: Tropical Storm Iselle Forecast Discussion Number 10
item.description:
Issued at 200 PM PDT Tue Aug 25 2026 
000
WTPZ44 KNHC 252041
TCDEP4
 
Tropical Storm Iselle Discussion Number  10
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP092026
200 PM PDT Tue Aug 25 2026

The structure of Iselle has significantly degraded during the past 
several hours, with the low-level circulation further detaching 
from the mid-level center located well to the northeast.  This 
change has caused any deep convection to be located well away from 
the center near the old mid-level center and is representative of 
a weakening cyclone.  A recent ASCAT scatterometer pass showed peak 
winds of about 45 kt, so the initial intensity is set to 50 kt, 
consistent with the low bias of the instrument.

Further weakening is anticipated due to continued shear, 
progressively cooler water and dry air entrainment near the core of 
the cyclone.  Perhaps because of the poor initial structure, 
Iselle isn't expected to be a particularly resilient cyclone, and 
no model shows organized deep convection beyond 36 hours.  The new 
NHC intensity forecast is lower than the last one, keeping the same 
general rate of weakening, but it shows a much earlier transition 
into a remnant low.
 
Satellite fixes show that the storm continues to move to the 
west-northwest, and little change in track is anticipated for the 
next couple of days due to ridging extending from the southern 
United States.  As the storm weakens, it should turn more westward 
by Thursday due to the cyclone becoming steered more by the 
low-level flow.  The guidance is shifting southward, consistent 
with a decaying system, so the new forecast is shifted equatorward, 
closest to the Google DeepMind ensemble mean.
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS
 
INIT  25/2100Z 21.0N 121.8W   50 KT  60 MPH
 12H  26/0600Z 21.3N 123.0W   40 KT  45 MPH
 24H  26/1800Z 21.8N 124.7W   35 KT  40 MPH

 60H  28/0600Z 23.5N 130.6W   25 KT  30 MPH...POST-TROP/REMNT LOW
 72H  28/1800Z...DISSIPATED

item.title: Remnants of Julio Public Advisory Number 5
item.description:
Issued at 200 PM PDT Tue Aug 25 2026 
312 
WTPZ35 KNHC 252038
TCPEP5
 
BULLETIN
Remnants Of Julio Advisory Number   5
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP102026
200 PM PDT Tue Aug 25 2026
 
...JULIO DISSIPATES...
...THIS IS THE LAST ADVISORY...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 200 PM PDT...2100 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...21.0N 119.5W
ABOUT 630 MI...1010 KM W OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...45 MPH...75 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...N OR 350 DEGREES AT 25 MPH...41 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1003 MB...29.62 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 200 PM PDT (2100 UTC), the remnants of Julio were located near 
latitude 21.0 North, longitude 119.5 West. The remnants are moving 
toward the north near 25 mph (41 km/h) and are expected to move 
northwestward into the circulation of Iselle tonight.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 45 mph (75 km/h) with higher gusts.
Weakening is expected as the remnants decay tonight.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 90 miles (150 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1003 mb (29.62 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
This is the last public advisory issued by the National Hurricane 
Center on this system.  For additional information on the remnants 
of Julio, please see High Seas Forecasts issued by the National 
Weather Service, under AWIPS header NFDHSFEPI, WMO header FZPN01 
KWBC, and on the web at ocean.weather.gov/shtml/NFDHSFEPI.php

 
$$
Forecaster Blake/Evans
item.author: nhcwebmaster@noaa.gov (NHC Webmaster)

item.title: Remnants of Julio Forecast Discussion Number 5
item.description:
Issued at 200 PM PDT Tue Aug 25 2026 
000
WTPZ45 KNHC 252040
TCDEP5
 
Remnants Of Julio Discussion Number   5
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP102026
200 PM PDT Tue Aug 25 2026

Satellite and microwave data indicate that the circulation of Julio 
has opened up into a trough of low pressure.  Thus, it is no 
longer a tropical cyclone, and this is the last NHC advisory.  The 
initial wind speed is set to 40 kt, consistent with the ASCAT-B pass 
from a few hours ago.  The remnant vorticity should wrap into the 
circulation of Tropical Storm Iselle and totally lose any identity 
soon.

For additional information on the remnants please see High Seas
Forecasts issued by the National Weather Service, under AWIPS
header NFDHSFEPI, WMO header FZPN01 KWBC, and on the web at
ocean.weather.gov/shtml/NFDHSFEPI.php
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS
 
INIT  25/2100Z 21.0N 119.5W   40 KT  45 MPH...REMNANTS OF
 12H  26/0600Z...DISSIPATED
 
$$
Forecaster Blake/Evans
